original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.

actual_scope: An exact ordered inverse for the nine-call paired-log controller, and the necessary and sufficient final-Y observation space for fixed linear decoding.
scope_change_reason: The new independent dirty-log local interface needs global scalar closure before native query pricing. This package proves that algebraic closure and identifies its remaining observations; it does not pass the positive native-budget gate.
bottleneck_link: Local centre replacements can leave source data encoded. The decoder identifies exactly which additional Y readers a complete supplier must price instead of assuming same-chart cancellation.
stop_rule: Finish the ordered proof, exact controls, source pins and focused contribution. Leave native acquisition and the broader constructive goal open.
evidence: Explicit decoder without an aggregate matrix inverse; equality of the initial-log and stacked-reader observation spaces; 290 exact input columns across common, mixed and noncommuting charts; 25 rejected corruption cases.
author: Jose Manuel (@jmbarrancoml)
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in proof, implementation and prose. Read-only mathematical agents supplied a first decoder derivation, independent controls and overlap checks. No independent human review.

open_questions.question: Can the four routed reader/update primitives fit the complete native budget?

open_questions.first_step: Implement one adjacent reader pair on actual Y-hole data, retaining owner maps, payload translations, injections and all paid changes.
open_questions.blocked_by: No priced native reader/update primitive follows from this scalar proof.

open_questions.why_it_matters: Four independent backward log blocks remain hidden in final Y under the present chronology.
open_questions.first_step: Identify a legal local operation that changes that hidden subspace and replay the altered data/log endpoint before pricing it.
open_questions.blocked_by: Reused logs and changed chronologies need new frame, independence and normalization proofs.
